description: Repurpose protein sequence diffusion models as guided samplers for multi-mutant generation. Start from the wild-type sequence, apply partial noising at mutable positions only, then denoise conditioned on structure and a stability-maximizing guidance signal. This generates diverse, high-quality mutation combinations in a single denoising pass.
mathematical_formalization: x_0 = wild-type, mask positions P = {p_1,...,p_k}. Forward: x_t[P] = noise(x_0[P], t). Reverse: x_{t-1}[P] = denoise(x_t, structure, t) + lambda * grad(f_stability(x_t)). Generate N samples, rank by f_stability.
analogical_connections: Classifier-guided diffusion in image generation (Dhariwal & Nichol 2021)
MCTD-ME: masked diffusion as rollout engine in MCTS
Langevin dynamics: gradient-guided stochastic energy landscape sampling
implementation_hypothesis: ESM-2 backbone, mask k positions, sample from masked LM with ProteinMPNN structure guidance. 256 parallel candidates on A100 (~10s). Score with combined oracle, return top-10.
experiment_seed: Generate 1000 multi-mutant candidates (k=5) for 20 proteins. Compare diversity, quality, and coverage vs beam search and MCTS. Ablate guidance lambda.
